description: Session recovery contract for ATLAS clients (web and the future Flutter app). Each vector is the sequence of POST /api/v1/auth/refresh responses a client sees after a request returned 401, and what the client must do. Web reference implementation: apps/web/src/lib/session-recovery.ts. Checked by apps/web/tests/unit/recovery-vectors.test.ts against the OpenAPI document and the web implementation.

vectors.web: Cookies were updated by the server; retry the original request once.
vectors.mobile: Save the new token pair to secure storage first, then drop the old pair from memory; retry the original request once.

vectors.web: Another tab rotated the shared cookies: wait 300–800 ms, retry the original request once without refreshing.
vectors.mobile: Re-read secure storage: if it holds a newer token (another isolate saved it), retry the refresh with it; if it is the same token, wait 1 s and retry the refresh once (a grace replay may succeed).

vectors.web: The retried request still got 401: make one more refresh; on success retry the request once more.
vectors.mobile: Same as V02; the second refresh attempt counts toward the limit of 3.

vectors.web: Go to /login?next=…&expired=1. Do not call logout.
vectors.mobile: Delete the local tokens without any server call and show login. Never present that token again (after 60 s it would count as reuse).
Delete the local tokens and show login; no retries.

vectors.web: Wait Retry-After plus a random 0–500 ms, then refresh again.
vectors.mobile: Same; the session and tokens are kept.

vectors.web: Show an inline 'server busy, retry' message; keep the session; no automatic refresh for 30 s.
vectors.mobile: Show an error banner; keep the tokens; no automatic refresh for 30 s.

vectors.web: Retry the same refresh after 1 s (the server replays a rotation for 60 s, so this is safe).
Retries after 1 s and 2 s, only within 45 s of the first attempt; then an offline message; keep the cookies; 30 s cool-down.
vectors.mobile: Show offline mode and keep the token. The next episode presents it once: if the lost request never reached the server it succeeds, otherwise REFRESH_REUSED and the user signs in again (accepted trade-off).
